title: truss plan.json, versions 1, 2 and 3
description: <truss dir>/plan.json: the seam between the design engineer, the PM and the hooks. The design engineer drafts it in plan mode; the PM owns it after that; the hooks treat it as read-only. See adr/0001-design-phase.md, section 8.

version.description: Plan file format version. It goes up whenever a field is added; readers gate on version >= 2, never === 2, so a later version inherits every v2 rule. Version 2 adds reworkAllowance. Version 3 adds the top-level goals array and a crew's goal.

goal.description: The run's goal, as the client gave it.

architecture.description: Repo-relative path of the architecture doc, as recorded in <repo>/.claude/truss.json.

approval.description: Set once, at plan time, by the design engineer's draft, and checked by the PM: "client" exactly when the plan has a stage-0 crew, otherwise "auto". Mid-run design slices never change it. The schema checks only that "client" implies a stage-0 crew, because the file can't show which crews a mid-run slice added.

approvedAt.description: An RFC 3339 date-time with a time-zone offset (JSON Schema format date-time), for example 2026-10-26T14:03:00+01:00 or 2026-10-26T13:03:00Z. A date-time with no offset is invalid. The design engineer's draft sets it: an "auto" draft carries the time the design engineer wrote the plan, which the PM overwrites with the time it logged the plan; an "client" draft carries null, which the PM replaces with the time the client approved. The allOf rule requires a string when approval is "auto". Null only while a run waits for the client; while approval is "client" and this is null, the run-level approval gate refuses every foreman in the plan.

agentCap.description: Deprecated and ignored since truss 0.7.0: nothing requires or enforces it. Still accepted so older plans validate. The total of the crews' estAgents isn't stored.

reworkAllowance.description: How many fresh QCs a crew may start after QC FAILs in this run. Required in version 2, forbidden in version 1. The design engineer copies it from reworkAllowance in <repo>/.claude/truss.json, or writes 2 when the key is absent. The same for every crew. See adr/0004-scope-repair-and-head-gates.md, section 5.

goals.description: Version 3 only. The goals added after the run's approval, in the order they were added. The run's first goal stays in the top-level goal, approval and approvedAt; its id is the reserved word "run". See adr/0010-mid-run-intake.md, section 1.

id.description: The goal's handle in /truss, in crews' goal field and in decisions.md tags. The crew-slug pattern, and never "run", which names the run's first goal.

goal.description: The goal as the client gave it.

addedAt.description: When the hook appended the goal: an RFC 3339 UTC date-time from its clock, ending in Z.

approval.description: "client" only when a client trigger in run/SKILL.md section 4 applies to the goal, otherwise "auto". A design crew alone does not make it "client".

approvedAt.description: Null until the PM logs the goal (auto) or the client approves it (client). While approval is "client" and this is null, the hooks hold the goal's crews.

allOf.$comment: Mirrors the top-level rule: an auto goal never waits, so an auto goal on disk fails the schema until the PM logs it.

maxParallelCrews.description: The most crews that may be running at once; extra crews in a stage queue. Default 4, from maxParallelCrews in <repo>/.claude/truss.json.

crews.description: One entry per crew. Within a stage, the order of this array is the queue order: crews beyond maxParallelCrews start in this order as running ones merge. The agent total is the sum of estAgents; it isn't stored.

allOf.$comment: versions 2 and 3 require reworkAllowance (ADR-0004 section 1, ADR-0010 section 1).
versions 1 and 2 forbid top-level goals and a crew's goal (ADR-0010 section 1). The schema can't check that a crew's goal names a goals entry; the hooks refuse a crew whose goal matches none.
approval "client" implies a stage-0 crew (ADR-0001 section 8). The reverse holds at plan time only, so it isn't checked.
approvedAt is null only while a run waits for the client, and an auto run never waits (ADR-0001 section 6).

slug.description: The crew's name, and the name of its truss:foreman: lowercase letters and digits in words joined by single hyphens, never ending in -<digits>. The -<digits> ending is reserved because a successor foreman is named <slug>-<n> and the hooks gate a successor as its base slug. safeName in hooks/register.ts leaves such a name of up to 100 characters unchanged, so report folders match the slug.

goal.description: Version 3 only, optional. The id of the plan goal the crew serves. Absent or "run" means the run's first goal; "run" needs no goals entry. The schema can't check that another value names a goals entry; the hooks refuse the crew when it doesn't.

stage.description: The stage the crew runs in. Stages are numbered per goal: an added goal's first stage is its stage 0. Stage 0 holds the change work and merges before any other stage starts; each stage merges before the next starts. A mid-run design slice goes to the earliest stage that hasn't started yet, and the crews that depend on it move one stage later.

verdict.description: What kind of crew this is. "design": writes ADRs and contract tests (a stage-0 crew, or a mid-run design slice). "change": a build crew whose module's design changed, so it runs after the design crew. "extend": a build crew working inside the existing design.

modules.description: Module names from the architecture doc's module map.

owns.description: Path globs the crew owns. No two crews may own the same file.

acceptanceTest.description: The command that proves the crew is done, runnable with the crew's own access.

acceptanceTestProved.description: Whether the design engineer ran acceptanceTest once while planning.

estAgents.description: Estimated agent count for the crew. The plan's agent total is the sum of these and isn't stored.

clientApproval.description: Optional; mid-run design slices only. The PM sets "pending" when the slice must wait for the client (one of the client triggers in ADR-0001 section 4 applies), and "approved" when the client answers. While it is "pending", the crew-level approval gate refuses this crew's foreman. Absent on every other crew.

status.description: Set by the PM as crews start and merge. The hooks only read it.

allOf.$comment: Stage 0 holds the change work: ADRs, the architecture-doc change and the contract tests (ADR-0001 section 5), which is what a design crew does (section 8). A change crew runs after the design crew, so it can't be in stage 0. A design crew may sit in a later stage: a mid-run slice goes to the earliest stage that hasn't started (section 7).
clientApproval is for mid-run design slices only (ADR-0001 sections 7 and 8).
